card.name: Verbs and words in old formal prose
card.fires_on: Mid-sentence words in older, formal essay prose, often a helping verb like be, was or has, or a noun like period, after a long subject. It also fires on a few unrelated URL or hyphen pieces.

modes.label: Helping verb after long subject
modes.description: A verb such as be, was or has follows a long subject in 18th and 19th century style writing.
modes.example: the number of representatives will<< be>> augmented from time to time in the manner

modes.label: Linking word in argument
modes.description: A noun or preposition inside a formal argument about numbers or national gains.
modes.example: the number was at a later<< period>> increased to twelve.

modes.label: Web address pieces
modes.description: A short letter chunk inside a web address or a K-8 style label.

card.plain: It lights up on small connecting words in old-fashioned formal prose, mostly after a long subject, and has no clear medical meaning.
